authority: Owner order of 2026-11-28: every build and every upgrade is staffed by a standing team of up to twenty specialist roles that work in parallel within the security and resource policy. This file is the one place to change that team: edit it, raise policy_version, and run python3 -m unittest tests.test_agent_team. A team listed here is a staffing plan; it does not start an agent.

intents_without_roster.audit: Read-only review by the gaie-verifier agent; no implementer team.
intents_without_roster.accelerate: Scoped pass: staffed from the route's workstreams, at most session_limit, until the owner adds a roster here.
intents_without_roster.repair: Scoped pass: staffed from the route's workstreams, at most session_limit, until the owner adds a roster here.
intents_without_roster.cinematic: Media pass: staffed from the route's workstreams, at most session_limit, until the owner adds a roster here.
intents_without_roster.release: Gated release under a separate owner approval; no implementer team.

concurrency.rule: The roster is how many specialists a plan staffs; concurrency is how many run at the same moment. effective = min(session_limit, cpus x agents_per_cpu); inside the workflow runner also min(cap, cpus - reserved_cpus). The first wave uses min(start, effective) agents. The live number is never above effective.

labels.session_limit: measured: the host refused agent calls past the twentieth
labels.agents_per_cpu: policy, not a measured optimum: chosen from host pressure at 11 and 16 concurrent agents on 4 CPUs
labels.start: policy: the first-wave size the economics recommender starts from
labels.workflow_runner: documented by the host and observed at 2 on a 4-CPU machine

evidence.contains: The host runs at most 20 agents at once

waves.order: Dependency waves of engineering_os.orchestrator.plan: team A first, teams B to F in parallel, then G, then H.
waves.size: A wave holds at most effective agents, one task per agent. A ready set larger than that runs as successive waves and is never started at once: 13 ready tasks on a 4-CPU host run 4+4+4+1 at the start size or 8+5 at the cap.
waves.next: engineering_os.economics.recommend_concurrency over the measured waves: stop on a limit error, halve on any conflict, grow only when verified tasks per million tokens improved, never above effective.

omission.rule: Every roster role is either staffed with at least one work item or listed in omitted with a reason. A role is never dropped silently, and a team never has more than session_limit roles.
omission.default_reason: no work item in this plan is assigned to this role

review.rule: The reviewer of a work item is never its producer. The first role with the registry's reviewer flag reviews; when that role produced the item, the first other testing reviewer does.

enforced_in_ci.claim: The policy loads only as strict JSON without duplicate keys and with schema_version, policy_version and implementation.
The role list equals governance/agent-roles.json and layers.ROLE_IDS, in order; the build and upgrade rosters are the full twenty.
No roster has more than session_limit roles, session_limit is never above 20, and an unknown, duplicate or missing mandatory role is refused.
Every concurrency number equals the evidence file it cites.
The orchestrator's session limit, agents per CPU and start come from this policy, and the router's maximum equals session_limit.
A staffing check refuses more than session_limit agents or an unknown role and lists every unstaffed roster role with a reason.
A wave never exceeds the host cap of min(20, CPUs x 2).
The reviewer of a work item is never its producer.
The specialist agent definition and its .claude mirror are identical, name this policy, and cannot start agents.

declared_only.claim: A live session starts the team this policy names.
declared_only.why: The lead session decides which agents to start; no code in this repository starts an agent.

declared_only.claim: An agent is the role it claims.
declared_only.why: Roles are caller assertions (governance/policies/orchestration.json authority); no identity provider authenticates them.

declared_only.claim: Live concurrency stays at or below effective.
declared_only.why: A session-level count guard needs a PreToolUse hook in .claude/settings.json, which is frozen (swarm/phase3/FREEZE.json), so none is installed. The host itself refuses agent calls past the twentieth (swarm/phase2/README.md finding 2).

declared_only.claim: A specialist writes only inside its work item's paths.
declared_only.why: agents/gaie-specialist.md instructs it and gives it no Agent tool; no hook confines its writes (docs/specs/gaie-20-layers/ORCHESTRATION.md section 9).

declared_only.claim: Sessions outside this repository follow this policy.
declared_only.why: An installed or vendored project carries the policy only once the bootstrap and the pack ship it with the router.
